diagnosis.root_cause: The EPON0/2 PON segment is down or failed, affecting the subscriber and other ONUs on the same port. All probed ONUs on EPON0/2 are offline with MPCP deregistration and no optical readings, while the OLT itself, router, VLAN, RADIUS, and subscriber authentication state are healthy.
evidence: The subscriber is currently offline, and zero/null RX and TX values are correctly interpreted as no reading rather than strong optical power.
The live ONU probe reports MPCP DEREG and Unaุth, which indicates loss of ONU registration rather than a RADIUS rejection.
Every ONU probed on EPON0/2 is offline and has no optical reading, showing a shared PON-level failure rather than an individual customer or fibre-drop fault.
The OLT health probe identifies a failed PON interface while the OLT remains reachable over ping and SNMP.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, router heartbeat, and VLAN state are normal, so there is no evidence of an OLT-wide, router, or provisioning failure.

Historical telemetry was stable at approximately -21 dBm RX, +2.3 dBm TX, 157 m distance, and healthy laser bias until the recent simultaneous loss of readings; this does not support fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
RADIUS records match CRM and session activity is normal, ruling out missing, suspended, conflicting, or flapping authentication as the cause.
The affected scope is the shared EPON0/2 PON port, with approximately 24 customers assigned to that port.

remediation.action: Escalate as a PON-port outage and inspect/reset EPON0/2 at the OLT. Check the OLT port optics, PON interface alarms, and feeder/splitter connection; reseat or replace the PON optic or move the affected customers to a spare PON port if the interface does not recover. After repair, verify that all ONUs re-register and that RX/TX readings return before closing the incident.

ground_truth.root_cause: All 24 customers on EPON0/2 lost service within the same minute. The OLT is healthy and its other two ports are serving normally, so the fault is confined to this PON port: the port optics, the feeder fibre or the primary splitter.
expected_reasoning: The subject ONU is offline with responds true and online 0
Probing the rest of EPON0/2 shows every ONU returning the same definite offline answer
All of them stopped within the same minute, which rules out coincidence
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, uptime is 77 days, and CPU, memory and temperature are at baseline
The other two PON ports on this OLT are serving customers normally
The failure boundary follows the port exactly, so the fault is the port and not the OLT
Signal history on the subject was flat and healthy until the cut-off, so this is not progressive degradation
PON port traffic has collapsed from its usual level to near zero
A whole port failing at once points to port optics, the feeder or the primary splitter
distractors: The health check still reports the OLT healthy because two of three ports pass
A single-customer complaint would frame this as an individual fault
